articles.title: Andrea Canning reports on the death of Sandra Birchmore in Canton, Massachusetts, in “The Betrayal of Sandra Birchmore" | Dateline
articles.summary: Watch the Dateline episode “The Betrayal of Sandra Birchmore" about the 2021 death of Sandra Birchmore in Canton, Massachusetts.
articles.body: Massachusetts native Sandra Birchmore’s life hadn’t been easy. Her teen years were difficult at times, and in an effort to make sure Sandra had some strong role models, her mother enrolled her in a program with the Stoughton Police Department. At 13 years old, Sandra was doing bootcamp drills and going on ride-alongs with law enforcement officers. She loved it, and even wanted to go into law enforcement at one point, but thought that with her asthma and being less than five feet tall she wouldn’t be able to. Instead, the 23-year-old was pursuing a teaching career. On a blustery afternoon in February 2021, the teacher’s assistant helped her students get out early so they could get home before an expected nor’easter blew into town. Three days later, when school resumed, Sandra didn’t show up to class. The school called police and asked for a welfare check. And their worst fears were confirmed when Sandra’s body was found in her apartment. There was no sign of a struggle. There was no sign of a break-in. To the responding officer, it seemed Sandra had taken her own life. To her co-workers and her family, it was a shock. Sandra had just shared happy news -- she was pregnant. The father, she told her family, was a Stoughton police officer. In fact, they would later learn, he had been one of the officers in that program she’d been in as a teen. So with such joy on the horizon, why would Sandra end her life? Her family didn’t think she had. And as the investigation pressed on, it became clear the FBI didn’t think so either... To find out what happened, watch the full episode “The Betrayal of Sandra Birchmore” on Peacock now. You can also watch on the NBC app or listen to it on our podcast. Watch Sandra’s friends and family remember her as a happy and bright young woman who always had a smile on her face. Plus, hear from Sandra Birchmore’s cousin Barbara Wright and a victim’s advocate named Mizzy Berry as they talk about the social media campaign and “stand outs” they’ve collaborated on to raise awareness about Sandra’s case. You can also listen to this week’s episode of Talking Dateline with Andrea Canning and Lester Holt, in which they take you behind the scenes of the episode.

articles.title: Josh Mankiewicz reports on the 2023 murder of Colorado mother Kristil Krug, in “The Phantom" | Dateline
articles.summary: Watch the Dateline episode “The Phantom" about the 2023 murder of Colorado mother Kristil Krug
articles.body: In the fall of 2023, Colorado mother Kristil Krug was getting more and more worried. She had been receiving text messages that were getting increasingly more intense. They started out as insulting and offensive, then turned more violent, darker. It was evident Kristil was being stalked. And the stalker was targeting her husband, too. She reported the stalking to Broomfield police, but by the time they identified her stalker — it was too late. Kristil had been murdered. And the investigation that followed was confounding… To find out what happened, watch the full episode “The Phantom” on Peacock now. You can also watch on the NBC app or listen to it on our podcast. Plus, watch Kristil’s family and friends remember her as a strong and confident woman. And, Kristil’s cousin Rebecca Ivanoff, a former prosecutor, discusses the dangers of stalking and coercive control, the warning signs to look for, and why making a safety plan and reaching out for help can save lives. Plus, a new law takes effect in Oregon that forces communications and social media companies to promptly comply with search warrants linked to stalking and domestic violence cases. You can also listen to this week’s episode of Talking Dateline with Josh Mankiewicz and Lester Holt, in which they take you behind the scenes of the episode.
